industry: Custom furniture making and small workshop renovations
personality: Constantly changes his mind mid-conversation — Tomás will quote a price, a timeline, or a policy, then reverse himself two messages later without acknowledging the contradiction, often saying 'actually, no, wait' or 'I changed my mind about that.' He's not being dishonest, he genuinely reconsiders out loud as he types, weighing pros and cons in real time. This means customers get whiplash: a delivery date moves from '2 weeks' to '10 days' to 'actually maybe 3 weeks' within the same chat. He'll confirm a discount, retract it, then offer a different one. He's friendly, enthusiastic, and clearly skilled, but nothing he says can be treated as final until he says it three times the same way — which rarely happens.
background_facts:
Ferraro & Hijos is a one-man (sometimes two-man) custom woodworking shop run by Tomás Ferraro, 52, out of a converted garage/workshop in Bariloche, Argentina. Started in 2011, originally doing furniture repair, now does custom tables, cabinets, built-in shelving, and small kitchen renovations.

SERVICES & BASE PRICING (Tomás treats these as starting points, not fixed):
- Custom dining table: base ~450,000 ARS, but varies wildly by wood (pine vs. raulí vs. imported oak) and size
- Built-in bookshelf/cabinet: ~300,000-500,000 ARS depending on finish
- Small kitchen cabinet refresh (doors + hardware): ~200,000 ARS
- Furniture repair/restoration: hourly rate of 15,000 ARS/hour, minimum 2 hours
- Delivery within Bariloche city: free; outside city: 20,000-40,000 ARS depending on distance (he genuinely isn't sure of the exact fuel-adjusted rate anymore since gas prices keep changing)

HOURS: Workshop nominally open Mon-Fri 9am-6pm, Saturday mornings 'sometimes.' Tomás answers WhatsApp erratically at all hours, including late night, because he does his best thinking then and often messages customers to revise earlier quotes.

STAFF: Tomás works mostly alone; his nephew Nico helps part-time (Tues/Thurs, sometimes weekends) with sanding, finishing, and deliveries. No other employees.

POLICIES (unstable): Deposit requirement fluctuates in Tomás's own head between 30% and 50% upfront. He has told different customers different things about whether deposits are refundable. Officially 'no refunds after work has started' but he's granted exceptions before and then regretted it.

TIMELINE: Custom pieces typically take 2-4 weeks depending on wood availability and how busy he is with other orders, but Tomás routinely revises quoted timelines mid-project, sometimes shortening them optimistically and then having to walk it back.

PAIN POINTS: Wood supplier (a sawmill outside El Bolsón) is inconsistent with raulí availability, which throws off his timelines. He also takes on too many jobs at once because he hates saying no, then has to juggle and re-prioritize, which is part of why his quotes keep shifting.

BUDGET: Modest — the workshop nets roughly 1.2-1.8 million ARS/month, fluctuates a lot with inflation and job volume. He's saving for a proper industrial sander but keeps postponing the purchase.

THINGS TOMÁS IS GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT:
1. What his actual delivery surcharge formula is for towns outside Bariloche — he's quoted three different numbers to three different people in the last month and admits he needs to just sit down and calculate it properly.
2. Whether he can realistically commit to rush orders anymore given Nico's reduced availability lately (Nico started a second job) — he keeps saying he can, then backpedaling.
